scope: the six functional-family lanes (clean, clojure, elixir, erlang, fsharp, haskell); the shape extends to any lane with an entry in script/m14/verify-grammar-pins.ts
rule: A pinned grammar is its wired bytes (sha256+length), its enumerable surface (id-order, type-set and field-set digests through web-tree-sitter, with the id/named/anonymous vocabularies recorded separately), the local copies those bytes are byte-identical to, the vendored source files (per-file sha256), and the authored provenance/decision record. Verification re-measures all of it and fails on ANY drift — including a vendored source edit, a vanished copy, or a name the vendored source declares that the wired wasm does not have. Regenerating the record is an explicit act (--write), never a silent side effect of verifying.

sourceVsWasm.note: the vendored tree carries no generated src/node-types.json + src/grammar.json pair, so the source↔wasm check cannot run for this lane; the recorded substitute is the measured surface delta against the base release's own wasm (see the decision's alternatives)

source.note: grammar.js + the split grammar modules (grammar/*.js) + src/ (scanner.c, grammar.json, node-types.json, unicode.h, tree_sitter/ headers) + package.json + tree-sitter.json + LICENSE + README.md, byte-for-byte from the npm tarball tree-sitter-haskell@0.23.1. The GENERATED src/parser.c (20 MB here) is deliberately not vendored: `tree-sitter generate` rebuilds it from grammar.js, and the source↔wasm check below runs on the generated JSONs, not on parser.c.

haskell.decision: Pin as-is: the wired wasm is byte-identical to the wasm published in tree-sitter-haskell@0.23.1, which is the newest release of tree-sitter/tree-sitter-haskell (the grammar is dormant at 0.23.1), and that tarball's source is now vendored in-tree with per-file hashes. No better candidate exists, locally or upstream.

elixir.decision: REPLACED the incumbent with upstream v0.3.5 (its npm tarball wasm; the sha256 is measured below). The incumbent was a 2024 prebuilt, byte-identical to tree-sitter-wasms@0.1.13's out/tree-sitter-elixir.wasm whose declared upstream dependency is tree-sitter-elixir ^0.1.1, and its only surface difference from upstream v0.3.5 was one anonymous token, `^^`, that upstream's source does not contain. That token was not inert: `x = ^^y` produced an ERROR node under the incumbent and parses cleanly under v0.3.5; both grammars agree on `1 ^^^ 2` and on single-caret pins. On the lane's two corpora the two builds produce identical trees on 773 of 773 files, so the upgrade costs nothing measurable and buys a named release, a vendorable source, and a wasm published by the grammar's own maintainers.

alternatives.measured: identical trees on 773/773 corpus files; carries a legacy `^^` token upstream removed, which mis-parses `x = ^^y` into an ERROR node
identical trees on 773/773 corpus files, 0 damaged files under both; cleaner `^^` handling; named release + vendored source

patches: grammar: adds `module_val_declaration` and `nullable_type` — exactly the two named types the wired wasm has that npm tree-sitter-fsharp@0.3.11's wasm does not

scanner: the manifest records an interface-probe patch with token-type lookahead; its SOURCE IS NOT IN-TREE (`common/scanner.h` is byte-identical to the npm 0.3.11 tarball's), so the patch is not reconstructible from this repo — recorded here rather than papered over

source.note: fsharp/grammar.js (the patched grammar — the npm tarball ships no grammar.js, so its vintage is fixed by hash here rather than by byte-identity to a tarball) + common/scanner.h (byte-identical to the npm 0.3.11 tarball) + package.json + tree-sitter.json + LICENSE + README.md. The vendored src/ holds only tree_sitter/ headers, which is why the source↔wasm check cannot run for this lane.

fsharp.decision: Pin the local rebuild. Three measured clauses: (1) the wired wasm's surface is upstream 0.3.11 PLUS exactly `module_val_declaration` and `nullable_type` and MINUS nothing; (2) the vendored grammar.js's rule set is 0.3.11's rule set plus exactly those two rules, with nothing dropped (fsharp-pin-evidence.json); (3) on the lane's own 400-file M12 sample the patch REPAIRS 9 files that unpatched 0.3.11 damages (e.g. infos.fs: 41 ERROR + 1 MISSING → 0/0) and damages exactly ONE that unpatched 0.3.11 parses clean (BasicProvider.Runtime.fs: an ERROR around `namespace` on line 5, after a `#if/#endif` block) — so the patch is a net parse win on real code with one recorded regression site. The claimed SCANNER patch still has no in-tree source and no minimal repro: two sample files show the claimed difference class in aggregate (fsharp-grammar-ab.json's sentinel hits), which is not the same as a repro, so it stays recorded-not-proven rather than asserted.

alternatives.measured: surface is a strict subset of the wired wasm's: missing module_val_declaration and nullable_type, carrying no type the wired one lacks
21 named types missing vs the wired wasm, 0 extra

source.note: no erlang grammar source exists on this machine (the npm name `tree-sitter-erlang` resolves to a security-holder placeholder). The pin is therefore bytes + surface fingerprint + the redistributor's own provenance table, not source.

erlang.decision: Pin the bytes with the strongest provenance available offline: the wired wasm is byte-identical to @lumis-sh/wasm-erlang@0.26.0, whose package metadata names WhatsApp/tree-sitter-erlang v0.15.0 at rev f21023bb built by tree-sitter CLI 0.26.7. Upstream is further along than v0.15.0, but no newer source or build exists locally, so an upgrade cannot be measured here and is not claimed.

provenance.chain: commit 34972a88 records the swap to @yogthos/tree-sitter-clojure 0.0.14 (a rewrite: list_lit/sym_lit/sym_name/sym_ns/vec_lit/kwd_lit/anon_fn_lit vocabulary, no interop nodes), after the canonical sogaiu 0.4.0 grammar failed 128/141 files of the clojure compiler's own source. No local package or source for the yogthos fork exists, so the spoken provenance cannot be re-derived here; the surface fingerprint below is the identity that CAN be checked.

source.note: the canonical sogaiu tree-sitter-clojure@0.4.0 source IS in the bun cache, but it is a DIFFERENT grammar from the wired wasm (the wired build's vocabulary is the fork's), so vendoring it would put a mismatched source in-tree next to the wired bytes — worse than no source. No yogthos source exists locally.

clojure.decision: Pin bytes + surface fingerprint + the commit that swapped them, and record the alternative that was measured and rejected: canonical sogaiu 0.4.0 failed 128/141 corpus files (34972a88), while the wired fork leaves 2 of 585 files damaged. A maintained fork (tree-sitter-clojure-orchard v0.2.8) is the obvious upgrade candidate but is unobtainable offline, so no claim is made about it.

alternatives.measured: 128/141 corpus files with grammar errors (from 34972a88); the wired fork: 2/585 damaged

provenance.chain: pinned v1.2.7 by commit 2bc64693 (wasm sha 9ea8525d, replacing 2b805890 of v1.2.4); that round verified the tracked source tree byte-identical to `git archive v1.2.7` through the production engine, with G1/G2 adjudication in reviews/m60-clean-grammar-127-adjudication.md. clean.decision: Keep v1.2.7 (already pin-verified by the clean round) and fold it into this registry so the family has one place that answers the question; for clean the answer is a sha + surface + a named adjudication rather than a vendored source.

provenance.chain: the wired bytes match no published prebuilt (neither tree-sitter-perl@1.2.1 nor @2.0.0 ships a wasm in its npm tarball, and tree-sitter-wasms@0.1.13/out has no tree-sitter-perl.wasm), so the build is recorded by sha + surface. Its SOURCE is now pinned: a fresh emcc build of the vendored tree-sitter-perl@1.2.1 source (emscripten/emsdk:3.1.64, `-shared -O2 -sSIDE_MODULE=1`) reproduces the wired idOrderDigest c954cfdc, typeSetDigest 61033c08 and fieldSetDigest d0e6aa8f exactly, and yields identical trees on 275/275 mojo files — the registry's own rule (two builds of one source agree even when their bytes differ), so the wired bytes ARE a build of 1.2.1's source. validation/m12/corpus-manifest.json already recorded the 1.2.1 upgrade; this entry makes it verifiable rather than asserted.

source.note: grammar.js + src/ (scanner.c, grammar.json, node-types.json, the tsp_*.h scanner headers, bsearch.h, tree_sitter/ headers) + package.json + LICENSE + README.md, byte-for-byte from the npm tarball tree-sitter-perl@1.2.1. The GENERATED src/parser.c (29 MB here) is deliberately not vendored, for the same reason as haskell's and elixir's: `tree-sitter generate` rebuilds it from grammar.js, and the source↔wasm check below runs on the generated JSONs, not on parser.c.

perl.decision: Pin as-is: the wired wasm is a build of tree-sitter-perl@1.2.1 — the newest release at the time this lane was first measured — proven by surface identity against a fresh build AND by 275/275 identical trees on the M12 pinned corpus, and that source is now vendored in-tree with per-file hashes so it cannot drift unnoticed. tree-sitter-perl@2.0.0 is the newer release and it is BETTER on the one axis this lane was weakest on (it removes the multi-child paren field that hid 39,897 payloads), but it is refused for this wave: it changes 123 of 275 trees on the M12 pinned corpus and would invalidate the M12 corpus claims and every other lane's pinned F5 row, and it buys the analyzer nothing it does not already have (identical emissions on 5,847 of 5,875 files). Take it as a scheduled grammar bump with a re-baseline, not as a silent swap.

alternatives.measured: identical trees on 275/275 mojo files vs a fresh 1.2.1 build; parse damage 4/275 files, 5 error nodes; the analyzer's fieldNodes() read recovers every payload the multi-child field hides, and 5,847 of 5,875 corpus files emit identically under 1.2.1 and 2.0.0

unreachable payload sites 39,897 -> 1,419 and affected files 3,049 -> 564 of 5,875; 36 of the 41 affected field pairs eliminated; parse damage unchanged at 4/275; but 123 of 275 mojo trees differ, and a parenthesised `use Module (...)` argument list carries no field at all in 2.0.0, so a field-driven import read sees nothing until the analyzer descends through the wrapper
